Devon H.: Quick share — ran the heatmap profiler vs prod-like burst test last night. Seeing a wide band of queueing delays ~30-80ms under steady load, but during bursts p95 stays ok while p99 shoots to 600-900ms. Correlated spikes with KV eviction churn and a kernel fallback event. Paste of the most relevant output below.

Devon H.: ```
# heatmap: x=time buckets, y=queue latency ms (percentile density)
00:00 - 00:05 | 10 12 17 22 36 48 300 820 900
00:05 - 00:10 | 9 11 15 20 33 40 280 610 870
00:10 - 00:15 | 12 14 18 24 38 55 320 700 940
notes: the high tail aligns with KV eviction logs and a kernel fallback from f16->q8-fallback.
```

Emma L.: Are these samples from the dedicated pool or the canary that uses pre-quantized kernels?

Devon H.: Dedicated pool, mixed model variants. Canary didn't have the pre-warm flag on; the fallback path occurs when the chosen kernel can't service the current sequence-length distribution and we fall back to the slower kernel (observed at ~T+3m into the burst). KV eviction rate increases when backlog > ~120 concurrent requests, eviction TTLs trash hot prefixes.

Emma L.: Any microbatch distribution data? p99 might be because a few very large microbatches get queued.

Devon H.: Yep — here's the microbatch histogram from the same run:```
microbatch_size: counts
1: 820
2: 410
4: 220
8: 95
16: 12
32+: 3
median=2, mean~3.1 but tail comes from 16+ when a backlog merges small requests into big microbatches while a slow kernel is active.
```

Ravi S.: Two quick ideas: adaptive microbatch ceiling + hot-prefix-aware batching.
Ravi S.: Proposed config (sketch):```
# adaptive batching policy
"min_batch": 1
"max_microbatch": 8  # start conservative
"burst_threshold": 100  # backlog requests
"ramp_step": 2  # increase ceiling by this when backlog persists > 5s
"prefetch_hot_prefixes": true  # use KV hints to avoid eviction misses
```
Ravi S.: The idea: during sudden bursts keep microbatch ceiling low to protect tail, then safely raise it as workers confirm stable kernel behaviour. Also avoid merging requests that touch different hot prefixes.

Lina T.: +1. Also consider a short pre-warm / keep-hot window for newly scaled workers. We saw a ~250ms cold-spin kernel init when the worker first receives a request (JIT-ish work + memory map + KV warm). Suggested policy: keep N=2 warm workers for each GPU for 30s after scale-to-zero, topped up with a burst-token bucket so very short bursts don't force scale-out.

Lina T.: Example burst-token config:```
burst_tokens: 50
refill_rate_sec: 10
keep_hot_after_burst_secs: 30
prewarm_workers: 2
```

Devon H.: Noted. The profiling trace shows the worst p99s occur when three conditions coincide: (1) high backlog merging into large microbatches, (2) KV eviction of those prefixes causing extra KV fetch latency (~80-120ms), (3) kernel fallback to a slower path. If we can break any leg we reduce tail massively.

deploy-bot: deploy v12/auto-scale-policy pushed to canary (eng-runtime-canary). No prewarm changes in this canary. Rollout at 2025-11-21T02:14:00Z.

Emma L.: For experiments I'd run a matrix: (A) adapt-batching only, (B) prewarm only, (C) both together, (D) control. Measure p95/p99 and also token cost delta.

Devon H.: Agreed. I'll run (A) and (B) concurrently on two separate canaries and capture 30m burst windows. Quick repro command I used: ```bash
./perf-burst --rps 1200 --dur 10m --seq-dist "mean=64,sd=16" --kv-hit=0.85
```

Ravi S.: Also can we instrument a tiny histogram for 'eviction-induced latency' per request (0/1 tag + extra ms) so we can attribute.

Devon H.: Good call — adding that to tracing.

Lina T.: Action items:
- Devon: run A/B canaries (A=adaptive microbatch ramping, B=prewarm + burst tokens) and upload heatmaps + per-prefix eviction traces.
- Ravi: prototype microbatch ceiling controller (10% CPU overhead budget).
- Emma: define evaluation criteria (p95/p99, cost delta, regressions on mean latency).

Devon H.: Setting tentative run for tonight 02:00 UTC. I'll post results in this thread. :rocket:

Emma L.: Thanks — if we see >2x p99 improvement on A or B we promote to staged rollout.

Ravi S.: I'll add a small feature-flag guard so we can toggle adaptive ramp per route.

Lina T.: ping me if you want me to tweak autoscaler cooldowns before runs.

Devon H.: Thanks, everyone. I'll attach the full traces once the runs finish.
